item_name: High-Risk Drug Classes: Use and Indication

lookback_source.quote: Column 1: Check if the resident is taking any medications by pharmacological classification during the 7-day observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

lookback_notes: 7-day look-back/observation period, or since admission/entry or reentry if the stay is less than 7 days. The manual uses the phrases "7-day look-back period" (e.g., N0415A1, B1, C1, D1, E1, F1, G1, H1) and "7-day observation period" (e.g., N0415I1, J1, K1) interchangeably for the same 7-day window; the Column 2 indication sub-items refer to "the observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days)." The document does not state how the 7 days are counted relative to the ARD within this section.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Code all high-risk drug class medications according to their pharmacological classification, not how they are being used.

source.quote: Code all high-risk drug class medications according to their pharmacological classification, not how they are being used.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Column 2 (Indication noted) is checked only if Column 1 is checked, and only if there is an indication noted for all medications in that drug class.

source.quote: Column 2: If Column 1 is checked, check if there is an indication noted for all medications in the drug class.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Code medications according to the medication's therapeutic category and/or pharmacological classification, not how it is used (e.g., oxazepam prescribed as a hypnotic is coded as an antianxiety medication, not a hypnotic).

source.quote: Code medications in Item N0415 according to the medication's therapeutic category and/or pharmacological classification, not how it is used.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Medications with more than one therapeutic category and/or pharmacological classification must be coded in all categories/classifications assigned to the medication, regardless of how it is being used (e.g., prochlorperazine is coded as an antipsychotic).

source.quote: Medications that have more than one therapeutic category and/or pharmacological classification should be coded in all categories/classifications assigned to the medication, regardless of how it is being used.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Include any of these medications given to the resident by any route in any setting (e.g., at the nursing home, in a hospital emergency room) while a resident of the nursing home.

source.quote: Include any of these medications given to the resident by any route in any setting (e.g., at the nursing home, in a hospital emergency room) while a resident of the nursing home.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Do not code antiplatelet medications such as aspirin/extended release, dipyridamole, or clopidogrel as N0415E, Anticoagulant.

source.quote: Do not code antiplatelet medications such as aspirin/extended release, dipyridamole, or clopidogrel as N0415E, Anticoagulant.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Anticoagulants such as Target Specific Oral Anticoagulants (TSOACs), which may or may not require laboratory monitoring, should be coded in N0415E, Anticoagulant.

source.quote: Anticoagulants such as Target Specific Oral Anticoagulants (TSOACs), which may or may not require laboratory monitoring, should be coded in N0415E, Anticoagulant.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Do not code flushes to keep an IV access patent in N0415E, Anticoagulant.

source.quote: Do not code flushes to keep an IV access patent in N0415E, Anticoagulant.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Code a medication even if it was given only once during the look-back period.

source.quote: Code a medication even if it was given only once during the look-back period.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Count long-acting medications (e.g., fluphenazine decanoate or haloperidol decanoate) given every few weeks or monthly only if they are given during the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: Count long-acting medications, such as fluphenazine decanoate or haloperidol decanoate, that are given every few weeks or monthly only if they are given during the 7-day lookback period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

federal_coding_rules.rule: For transdermal patches, capture the medication only if the patch was applied to the resident's skin during the observation period.

source.quote: To code N0415, only capture the medication if the transdermal patch was applied to the resident's skin during the observation period.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Combination medications should be coded in all categories/pharmacologic classes that constitute the combination (e.g., a single tablet combining an antipsychotic and an antidepressant is coded in both categories).

source.quote: Combination medications should be coded in all categories/pharmacologic classes that constitute the combination.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Over-the-counter sleeping medications are not coded as hypnotics, as they are not categorized as hypnotic medications.

source.quote: Over-the-counter sleeping medications are not coded as hypnotics, as they are not categorized as hypnotic medications.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Herbal and alternative medicine products (e.g., melatonin, chamomile, valerian root) are dietary supplements and should not be counted as medications.

source.quote: Therefore, they should not be counted as medications (e.g., melatonin, chamomile, valerian root).

federal_coding_rules.rule: When N0300 (Injections) is coded 0, skip to N0415, High-Risk Drug Classes: Use and Indication.

source.quote: If 0 → Skip to N0415, High-Risk Drug Classes: Use and Indication

federal_coding_rules.rule: Example application: a PRN antipsychotic received with a documented indication is coded in both Column 1 and Column 2; a hypnotic received without a noted indication is coded in Column 1 only (Column 2 not checked).

source.quote: N0415D1. Hypnotic = checked; temazepam is a hypnotic medication. N0415D2. Hypnotic = not checked; indication for use of temazepam was not noted.

federal.criterion: Review the resident's medical record for documentation that any of these medications were received by the resident and for the indication of their use during the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: Review the resident's medical record for documentation that any of these medications were received by the resident and for the indication of their use during the 7-day lookback period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

federal.criterion: Review documentation from other health care settings where the resident may have received any of these medications while a resident of the nursing home (e.g., valium given in the emergency room).

source.quote: Review documentation from other health care settings where the resident may have received any of these medications while a resident of the nursing home (e.g., valium given in the emergency room).

federal.criterion: An "indication" is the identified, documented clinical rationale for administering a medication, based upon a physician's (or prescriber's) assessment of the resident's condition and therapeutic goals.

source.quote: The identified, documented clinical rationale for administering a medication that is based upon a physician's (or prescriber's) assessment of the resident's condition and therapeutic goals.

federal.notes: Definition box; governs whether Column 2 can be checked.

federal.criterion: Assessors should be able to identify the source(s) used to support coding of pharmacological classification on the MDS 3.0; facilities may wish to identify a resource their staff consistently use.

source.quote: Facilities may wish to identify a resource that their staff consistently use to identify pharmacological classification as assessors should be able to identify the source(s) used to support coding the MDS 3.0.

federal.notes: Framed as a suggestion ("may wish") but with an expectation that the source can be identified.

federal.criterion: Assessors should consult the manufacturer's package insert for pharmacological classification and may work with the resident's pharmacist to confirm medication classification(s).

source.quote: Assessors should consult the manufacturer's package insert, which may contain the medication's pharmacological classification.

federal.criterion: When a resident receives antipsychotic, antianxiety and hypnotic medications simultaneously there must be a clear clinical indication; adequate documentation is essential in justifying their use.

source.quote: Administration of these types of medications, particularly in this combination, could be interpreted as chemically restraining the resident. Adequate documentation is essential in justifying their use.

federal.notes: Stated in a note following the coding example.

federal.criterion: Providers are responsible for coding each medication's pharmacological/therapeutic classification accurately; the listed external resources are optional and not required for MDS completion.

source.quote: Providers are responsible for coding each medication's pharmacological/therapeutic classification accurately.

case_mix_relevance.notes: The N0415 section of this document does not tie the item to any payment or case-mix classification.

conflicts.topic: Terminology for the 7-day window across N0415 sub-items ("look-back period" vs "observation period")

positions.claim: Several sub-items describe the window as the "7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days)."

source.quote: N0415A1. Antipsychotic: Check if an antipsychotic medication was taken by the resident at any time during the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

positions.claim: Other sub-items describe the window as the "7-day observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days)."

source.quote: N0415J1. Hypoglycemic (including insulin): Check if a hypoglycemic medication was taken by the resident at any time during the 7-day observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

conflicts.resolution: Terminological only — both phrases describe the same 7-day window; recorded for transparency, no substantive difference stated in the document.
